meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.trans: I would think about it.
I'd buy a house.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: 'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.trans: Go and hire Galileo.
Take the money.

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.
examples.trans: Then go and hire Galileo.

meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать').

examples.text: В этом году все квоты выбрали.
examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.
She chose the most beautiful dress.
Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

ехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride

meanings.en: to go, to drive, to ride
meanings.note: by car, bus, train, in one direction, now
'едем' = we're going / let's go. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride', paired with 'поехать'.

examples.trans: Vitalik, we're going to the Santa Fe.
Let's go!

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!
This is my wife.
I'm with my wife this evening.

examples.text: Но вечером я обещал быть с женой.
examples.trans: But I promised to be with my wife this evening.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She is a wise woman.
Who is that woman?

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative.
+ instrumental.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose.

examples.trans: What have you come for?
What's that for?
Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Пятьдесят метров, не больше. Иначе будет сигнал.
examples.trans: Fifty metres, no more. Otherwise there'll be a signal.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Стоять на коленях = to kneel.

examples.trans: I'm on my knees.

examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

meanings.note: + infinitive.

examples.trans: I can't today.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: From the tax inspectors and the fire inspectors!

meanings.en: to be rude to, to insult (someone)
meanings.note: + dative: нахамить кому-то. Perfective of хамить.

meanings.en: to offend, to hurt someone's feelings

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Простые люди = ordinary people.

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.en: to sort out, to settle, to deal with
meanings.note: мы сами разберёмся = we'll sort it out ourselves
В + prepositional.

examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: informal: a group of young men; ребята! = guys!

meanings.note: Of a door, bag, etc.
Diminutive of рука.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами.

справиться.gloss: to manage, to cope, to handle

meanings.note: often + с + instrumental, or used absolutely

examples.trans: We won't manage here in two years.

examples.text: Конечно, не справитесь. Вы же не я.
examples.trans: Of course you won't manage. You're not me, after all.

examples.text: Мы обязательно справимся и с этим.

meanings.note: As opposed to before.

examples.trans: Now I'm the boss.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?

тянуть.gloss: to pull; to drag out, to delay

meanings.note: тянуть с + instrumental, colloquial
Меня тянет к нему = I'm drawn to him.

examples.trans: Don't drag it out!
Don't delay your answer.

examples.text: И не тяни с торговым центром!
examples.trans: And don't drag your feet with the shopping centre!

meanings.note: adjective/participle used in formal address

examples.trans: Esteemed veteran, listen to me.

examples.text: Уважаемый ветеран, перед вами внук предателя!
examples.trans: Esteemed veteran, before you is the grandson of a traitor!

meanings.note: Уволен = fired (short participle).

examples.trans: You're fired!
He was fired.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.
Is he being rude to you?

examples.text: Он что, действительно посмел открыто хамить тебе в зале?

examples.text: Хороший официант никогда не станет хамить даже трудному гостю.
examples.trans: A good waiter will never be rude even to a difficult guest.

examples.text: Выбрала попроще кого-нибудь! Всё, нам хана теперь.
examples.trans: You should have picked someone simpler! That's it, we're done for now.
If the chef finds out, you're toast.
A good day.
What a lovely morning!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: русским языком сказать = say in plain Russian
Organ in the mouth.

examples.trans: I told you in plain Russian.
He knows the Russian language well.

examples.text: А ты не кричи на меня! Я тебе русским языком сказала.
examples.trans: Don't you yell at me! I told you in plain Russian.
